notes.1: The majority of candidates gave the correct response.
notes.2a: The best responses were able to provide an accurate definition.
notes.2b: (i), (ii) and (iii) These questions were answered well by the majority of candidates.
notes.2biv: Most candidates answered this question well, and many gave a complete explanation and made reference to the correct feeding relationships. A common error was to describe the effect on organisms other than the starfish and the limpets
notes.2v: Some candidates were able to provide the correct responses but some found this a challenging question.
notes.2c: Many were able to correctly identify the principal source of energy. Common errors were producers, algae, phytoplankton, and water.
notes.2d: Many candidates showed a good understanding of the water cycle. Most correctly identified B and D, fewer could identify process C. A common misconception was to identify A as evaporation.
notes.3a: The majority of candidates showed a good understanding of this topic. Less confident responses were unsure of how to classify female sterilisation, vasectomy and IUD.
notes.3b: Many candidates provided good responses to this question. A common error was to substitute ‘enzymes’ for ‘hormones’.
notes.3c: (i) This proved challenging for many with only a few able to correctly state the full name.
notes.3cii: A good understanding was shown by the majority of candidates. Common correct responses were sharing needles and sexual intercourse.
notes.3iii: A good understanding was shown by the majority of candidates. Common correct responses were not sharing needles, the use of condoms and avoiding blood to blood contact.
notes.4a: The petal was correctly labelled by most candidates. Identification of the stigma was challenging for some.
notes.4b: This proved to be challenging form some candidates. A common error was to provide features of the flowers rather than the pollen.
notes.4c: A few candidates were able to correctly identify the process involved.
notes.4d: This was well answered. Functions of the ovary and petal were common correct responses.
notes.5a: (i) Some were able to correctly identify the structure. Common errors were to identify tissue A as epidermis or cuticle and cell B as a stoma(ta).
notes.5aii: This was well answered by the majority of candidates.
notes.5b: Most candidates answered this question well. Cell wall and permanent vacuole were the most frequent incorrect responses.
notes.5c: Many were able to recall the reactants for photosynthesis. Some responses provided only one reactant or gave the products of the reaction.
notes.5d: Some were able to describe good explanations for their choice of leaf and made reference to the diagram provided.
notes.6a: This was well answered by most candidates. In general candidates were familiar with alcohol and tobacco, less so with the effects of heroin.
notes.6b: (i) and (ii) The majority of candidates were able to give good responses to these questions.
notes.6biii: This question asked for a description not an explanation. Many were able to provide a good description and included a data quotation in their response.
notes.6c: This proved to be a challenging question with some giving specific examples of infections rather than the type of microorganism that is affected by antibiotics.
notes.7aii: A challenging question for some. A common error was to give the value per ten minutes rather than per minute.
notes.7iii: Some candidates provided good responses. A common error was to describe transpiration rather than the movement of the air bubble.
notes.7b: Most responses identified where water enters a plant, fewer could recall the process involved.
notes.7c: This proved challenging for many. Better responses showed a good understanding of what processes were involved and where in the plant they occurred.
notes.8a: Well answered. A common error was to name specific foods rather than the component groups to which they belonged. For example a named meat was given rather than protein.
notes.8b: Some candidates were able to recall the specific part of the alimentary canal.
notes.8c: Some candidates were able to correctly identify the structures labelled on the excretory system diagram. The spelling of words like ureter and urethra must be accurate.
notes.8d: The majority of candidates answered this question well.
notes.key_messages:
Read all questions carefully and answer the question asked. See Questions 4(b) and 7(a)(iii).
Command words such as ‘describe’, ‘explain’, ‘suggest’ and ‘compare’ require different responses.
Candidates should be encouraged to identify the differences in requirement for command words and in
particular the difference between ‘explain’ and ‘describe’ questions.
Where a description of a graph or table of data is required, it is expected that data will be quoted (with units
where appropriate) in the description given. Many candidates are able to do this effectively.
Where numbered answer lines are given there should be only one response on each numbered line.
notes.general_comments: Many excellent scripts were seen and a good understanding of many areas of the syllabus was shown.
